runs: There are so many good conversations happening on >x<, it may be hard to find what’s most relevant to you from time to time. That’s where Topics can help.

From your profile menu, on your Home timeline, and in search results, you’ll see prompts to follow various Topics. Simply follow the Topic and we'll personalize your >x< experience with relevant posts, events, and ads. We may also match you with other Topics that we think you are interested in based on your profile and activity, such as the posts you view or like.

runs: How we select Topics

There are numerous Topics across many categories on >x< to follow. We’re working hard to add new Topics all the time. How do we choose which Topics to offer? They’re based on the volume and health of conversations happening on >x<. For volume, we look at how much people are posting, Reposting, replying, and liking posts about that Topic.

We want Topics on >x< to reflect the broader, lasting conversations people have about the events, people, and things they discuss. So we use machine learning to find related posts from these conversations. This could mean they post a lot about the Topic or interact a lot with posts about the Topic. From there, we find the posts that are most interesting to those people, using algorithms, keywords, and additional signals.

We’ve implemented a number of protections to help keep conversations included in a Topic healthy and free from abuse — including working to not recommend posts for a Topic if the engagement is manipulated or spammy.

Just like with accounts you follow, you can unfollow Topics at any time. Go here for steps on unfollowing a topic. We may still occasionally recommend Posts about a particular Topic, for example, if you continue to like, Post, or repost about it. When you unfollow a Topic, we will no longer suggest content based on the fact that you followed that Topic.

q: How do I opt out of interests that don't reflect what I’m into?

. We won’t use that Topic to personalize your experience on >x<, and we will not recommend it as one you can follow in the future, unless you specifically search for it. Please note that these changes can take some time to take effect across our systems, and you may still see content about a Topic due to other reasons such as following someone who is talking about it.

As we continue to build new Topics, including Topics that may involve more complex subjects and interests, we may take a cautious approach by only featuring a limited amount of accounts to start before adding more over time. We do this to test out the Topic and adjust our systems so we’re serving you the most interesting, healthy posts.
If you have a comment, question, or concern about the curated content you see on Topics, let us know.
